the failure to test for stimulus equivalence relations in Phase 1 prevented their resurgence when the relations inconsistent with Phase 1 were extinguished in Phase 2.

the failure to observe resurgence of past equivalence classes when extinction of new equivalence classes is followed by a test of past equivalence classes suggests that the equivalence-testing procedure is a critical component of equivalence-class formation.
the extinction of untested derived stimulus classes did not produce resurgence of untested derived relations.

the conditions that are necessary and sufficient to establish stimulus equivalence, which is important for understanding the formation of these stimulus relations.
the necessary conditions that establish derived relations.
the role of equivalence testing in establishing equivalence classes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the context of testing is necessary to establish derived stimulus relations, and that the context of reinforcement is necessary for the establishment of derived stimulus relations that have a functional relation to reinforcement.
the stimulus relations that are derived in the context of an equivalence-testing procedure are the result of the operant behavior that occurs during this procedure.
the operant nature and the necessary and sufficient variables that establish derived stimulus relations remain unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stimulus equivalence relations are not formed in isolation, but rather, they are formed in a specific context that includes the testing of these relations.
the context for equivalence testing is a necessary condition for establishing equivalence relations.
the context of equivalence testing is an important factor in establishing derived stimulus relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stimulus relations that occur in extinction may be limited to those that have been tested previously.
the stimulus relations that emerge in equivalence classes are not established by the training that establishes baseline discriminations.
the stimulus equivalence relations that occur in a given context are not simply those that are consistent with the context.
